question: A user types text into a sidebar search input inside app/dashboard/layout.tsx and then clicks a link from /dashboard/billing to /dashboard/settings. What happens to the search input?
options: The input clears because Next.js unmounts all layouts on every route change
The input value and DOM element are preserved because nested layouts stay mounted across sibling navigations
Next.js throws a hydration error unless the input is moved into template.tsx
The input clears unless you wrap it in 'use client' and localStorage
explanation: With partial rendering, shared layouts like app/dashboard/layout.tsx stay mounted while only the changing child page swaps, preserving React state and DOM nodes across sibling routes.

question: When a folder contains both layout.tsx and template.tsx, in what order do they wrap page.tsx?
options: template.tsx wraps layout.tsx, which wraps page.tsx
layout.tsx wraps template.tsx, which wraps page.tsx
Next.js forbids placing layout.tsx and template.tsx in the same folder
explanation: A segment's layout.tsx always renders on the outside and wraps template.tsx, which in turn wraps the segment's page.tsx or nested child routes.

question: Which scenario is the clearest reason to choose template.tsx instead of layout.tsx?
options: Keeping a persistent audio player running while users browse different albums
Re-triggering a CSS enter animation and resetting local feedback form state on every page visit
Defining the root <html> and <body> tags for the application
Rendering a shared navigation sidebar whose scroll position should never reset
explanation: Because template.tsx mounts a brand-new React instance on every route transition, local state resets and mount effects/animations re-run automatically per visit.

question: Which statement about nested layout.tsx files is true?
options: Every nested layout.tsx must also render its own <html> and <body> tags
A layout can pass props directly to its children like React.cloneElement(children, { user })
Only the root app/layout.tsx defines <html> and <body>; nested layouts wrap children with normal semantic elements
Nested layouts are ignored unless the parent folder has a page.tsx
explanation: Only the root app/layout.tsx renders <html> and <body>. Nested layouts wrap children in regular elements such as <section> or <div> and do not pass direct props to children.
